title: A garden, a beginning
excerpt: What if a personal website could feel like opening a door?
body: This garden starts with a question: what if a website could hold a little more of a person? Not only what they do, but what they notice, where their curiosity takes them, and what they are still trying to understand.

The spaces here give those different interests somewhere to live. A library for ideas still unfolding. An observatory for places on the horizon. A gallery for looking closely. A laboratory for asking what might happen next.
The garden itself connects them. Warm materials meet new tools; old patterns make room for new possibilities. It is an invitation to wander, and to leave a little space for the unexpected.

title: The shape of light
excerpt: An Orosi window changes a room without moving a wall.
body: Light through colored glass makes a room feel different from one hour to the next. The architecture remains still, but its atmosphere keeps moving.
That small transformation is a starting point for this digital space: a place that responds quietly to your presence, where movement is an invitation rather than a demand.

The most interesting detail may be the one you almost pass by. A reflection, a grain of wood, a line that repeats until it becomes a pattern. Looking a little longer can be its own kind of exploration.

title: Room for the unfinished
excerpt: A place for questions before they become answers.
body: A digital garden can make room for unfinished thinking. An experiment does not need to become a product to be worth sharing; a question does not need an immediate answer to be worth keeping.
This room is for that middle ground: things being learned, connections being noticed, and ideas that might turn into something entirely different.
These introductory essays describe the concept of this garden. Personal writing will take their place as the collection grows.
